name: Kot Addu

queries.query: Pakistan official cadastral parcel map GIS Kot Addu Muzaffargarh land records map
queries.result: First-party discovery identified the Punjab Land Records Authority public land map and the PULSE land-system map. The official PLRA viewer exposes a Punjab cadastral ArcGIS service with a named Kot Addu polygon layer.

queries.query: پاکستان کوٹ ادو کاداستر نقشہ پارسل زمین ریکارڈ سرکاری
queries.result: Urdu discovery did not expose a separate local Kot Addu registry endpoint. The first-party Punjab PLRA/PULSE map services were independently reachable and provide the evidenced cadastral layer.

registryCustodian.name: Punjab Land Records Authority (PLRA), Government of Punjab, with PULSE map services
registryCustodian.scope: Punjab-wide land-record and cadastral-map services; the public map service has a dedicated Kot Addu polygon layer. This does not establish legal title or complete citywide coverage.

localCustodianContext.name: Municipal Committee Kot Addu / PULSE local mapping context
localCustodianContext.scope: The municipal base-map publication identifies parcel boundaries and was prepared by the Municipal Committee Kot Addu GIS Officer; it is cartographic context, not a qualified parcel API.

service.name: PLRA Punjab Cadastral Maps ArcGIS Feature Layer — Kot Addu
service.viewerConfiguration: The current PLRA viewer JavaScript names the Punjab_Cdastral_Maps service and the Kot Addu layer (layer 16). Anonymous service metadata describes a polygon Feature Layer supporting JSON/GeoJSON/PBF queries.

schemaAndCrs.geometryCrs: EPSG:3857 (source; samples requested as EPSG:4326 GeoJSON)

requestsAndEndpointChecks.outcome: Public PLRA/PULSE viewer loaded. Its current JavaScript exposed the PLRA ArcGIS service, Kot Addu layer, and public token route; login is required for complete parcel details in the UI, and no login was attempted.
Anonymous public viewer token endpoint returned a short-lived service token; it was used only for bounded public map metadata/query requests and is not retained.
Without the viewer token the service returned ArcGIS 499 Token Required; no bypass was attempted.
With the anonymous public viewer token, layer metadata verified Kot Addu, polygon geometry, native OBJECTID, Shape geometry, EPSG:3857, maxRecordCount 2000, and GeoJSON support.
Exact-point-centered 600 m web-mercator envelope returned zero features. This is an exact bounded probe only and is not evidence of citywide absence.
Wider local probe returned native OBJECTIDs, confirming bounded local layer availability without requesting unsafe fields.
Independent bounded native-ID geometry read returned three complete polygons retained in kot-addu-parcel-samples.geojson with only canonical id properties.
PULSE data hierarchy endpoint required authentication; no credentials or bypass was attempted.
The viewer exposes a download route, but no Mauza was selected and no download or ownership data was requested.

scopeLimits: The exact WUP point [30.4674951563177, 70.9680706614739] was preserved in latitude/longitude order and was not shifted.
The exact-point-centered 600 m query returned zero features; the wider local query returned features and is the relevant bounded availability evidence.
The layer is a public cadastral-map representation; it does not establish legal title, ownership, address, contact, tax, account, or citywide completeness.
Native source fields other than OBJECTID were not requested or retained; no unsafe fields were requested.
Packet completion is research completion only and is not source integration or admission.
uncertainty: The public viewer reports login for complete parcel details and its hierarchy/download endpoints require authentication; only the anonymous public map layer was qualified.
The wider local probe demonstrates nearby Kot Addu layer records but does not prove every urban or district parcel is covered.
No independent serial reviewer has qualified a runtime adapter.
